## Metrics

**localisation** (`time_s, ticks, path_length_m, min_clearance_m, mean_clearance_m, heading_change_rad, contacts, expansions, plans, final_goal_distance_m, final_err_xy_m, final_err_yaw_rad, mean_err_xy_m, max_err_xy_m, converged_s, recovery_s, compute_ms`):

- `final_err_xy_m / final_err_yaw_rad`: $\lVert \hat p - p \rVert$ and $|\mathrm{wrap}(\hat\theta - \theta)|$ at the end (belief vs truth)
- `mean_err_xy_m / max_err_xy_m`: over the error sampled every 1 s
- `converged_s`: first time from which 5 consecutive samples have error < 0.5 m and < 0.3 rad
- `recovery_s`: (kidnap) the same, counted from the kidnap
- `success`: the robot reached the goal AND the final error is < 0.5 m and < 0.3 rad

`compute_ms` is wall time on the running device, reported but never compared across devices and never part of a hash.

## Held-out scenarios

6 per evaluation; ADR 0014 (secret salt, per head) in CI; R2 public salt locally.

## Known biases and limitations

- **MODEL, kinematic.** Differential-drive planar kinematics with terrain following; no dynamics, contact forces, friction or tipping (AGENTS.md invariants). A success here is not a success on hardware; the R3 Gazebo + Nav2 subsets measure how far it carries to a full ROS 2 stack in simulation (STACK), still not hardware.
- **One robot, one robot model** (COCO: radius 0.22 m; inflation radius 0.25 m in the planning costmap). No multi-robot interaction.
- **No hardware.** No physical robot exists; nothing here is a REAL ROBOT RESULT.
- **Synthetic worlds.** The Proving Ground and the Depot are authored worlds (World Spec), not scans of real buildings.
- **Generator bias.** Scenarios are drawn from free cells with clearance > 0.35 m and must be connected on the planning grid; start or goal in tight spots and unreachable goals are therefore absent by construction. Filtered suites keep a scenario only if the reference A* path passes the filter, which biases them towards what A* finds.
- **Reference-path features.** Tiers depend on A*'s path on the default costmap; another planner may find the same scenario easier or harder.

## Versioning

Frozen: a change to any scenario, condition or the world is a new version (`<id>.v2.json`); results name the suite version, the model hash version (3), the experiment schema and the algorithm API they were made with. v0 files stay as they are.
